mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds Rate above 5.25% in a given month coincides with a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return due to higher discount rates eroding expected equity future cash flows.
failure_condition: Over a 12-month window, 20-day forward returns remain non-negative during high-rate periods, or the rate spike is not statistically significant (Granger causality p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly payrolls increase (PAYEMS) exceeding 150,000 jobs while unemployment (UNRATE) remains below 3.5% signals a strong labor market, which precedes a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return via optimism about growth.
failure_condition: Across 5 consecutive months meeting the trigger, 60-day forward returns are not statistically outperforming a baseline model (F-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive monthly decline in industrial production (INDPRO) of more than 2% followed by a rebound above the prior month's level predicts a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as it signals a bottoming in supply-side weakness.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO drops > 2% in month t AND INDPRO[t+1] > INDPRO[t]
failure_condition: The pattern recurs but is not followed by a positive 20-day return (lagged returns IC < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly rise in consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) above 4% for two consecutive months indicates accelerating inflation, which is associated with negative 5-day S&P 500 forward returns as investors anticipate rate cuts soon.
failure_condition: Over 6 months of inflation above 4%, 5-day forward returns remain non-negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in residential housing starts (HOUST) by more than 10% in a month coincides with a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return as it signals a cooling housing market and reduced economic momentum.
failure_condition: The monthly drop is not statistically significant (Granger causality p > 0.05) or is followed by a positive 20-day return.

mechanism_narrative: When unemployment falls below 3% for three consecutive months while payrolls (PAYEMS) remain flat, it creates a labor market overhang that precedes a negative 60-day S&P 500 forward return as profit-taking intensifies.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 3% for 3 months AND PAYEMS flat
failure_condition: Over the 60-day window, forward returns are not statistically negative relative to a no-change baseline (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A two-month decline in retail sales (not available in the provided proxies; fallback to RSAFS as a proxy for demand) followed by a rebound above the prior month's level predicts a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as demand recovers.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS falls > 5% in month t AND RSAFS[t+1] > RSAFS[t]
failure_condition: The pattern recurs but is not followed by a positive 20-day return (IC < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in the 10-year Treasury yield (not available in proxies; fallback to FEDFUNDS behavior as a proxy for expectations) below 3% for 4 consecutive months predicts a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return as lower discount rates boost equity valuations.
failure_condition: The low-rate condition persists but forward returns over 60 days are not significantly higher than during a neutral-rate period (p > 0.05).
